## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Across eight quarters the story is strikingly **linear and self-consistent** — rare for biotech. EPKINLY sBLA in 2L follicular lymphoma accepted (PDUFA 30-Nov-2025); **EPCORE-FL1 hits both primary endpoints** (PFS HR 0.21 — a 79% risk reduction, genuinely best-in-class). Rina-S endometrial data (50% ORR vs ~15% SoC). Acasunlimab pushed into melanoma. The wholly-owned engine is now *de-risking*, not just spending.

A *third* multibillion-dollar wholly-owned pillar. GEN1042 (head & neck) killed in the same breath — discipline maintained even while doing a transformative deal. Funded by a **$5.5B debt offering** (first material leverage in the company's history).
- **Feb-2026 (FY25):** Merus closing telegraphed for early Q1-26. 2026 framed as "a defining year" — *up to 6 potentially registrational readouts*. The one blemish surfaces: **EPCORE-DLBCL-1 monotherapy** hit PFS but **OS did not reach statistical significance** — management contextualizes (COVID, salvage-therapy availability) and insists it "does not change expectations" for the other trials.

**Drivers introduced and kept:** EPKINLY franchise expansion (3L→2L→1L), Rina-S indication-laddering (ovarian→endometrial→PSOC→lung/GI), wholly-owned commercial build-out (US→Japan→EU). **Drivers quietly dropped:** acasunlimab has *faded* from the front of the narrative — loud in 2024 ("unprecedented OS data," full control taken), it is now a secondary melanoma/NSCLC signal-seeker barely mentioned by Q1-26.
